data.title: Erythromycin (oral + topical)
data.summary: Other antibacterials · Macrolide antibiotic (14-membered lactone ring; prototype macrolide)
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Other antibacterials_

**Class:** Macrolide antibiotic (14-membered lactone ring; prototype macrolide)

## Mechanism of action
- Binds 23S rRNA of the 50S ribosomal subunit → blocks translocation → bacteriostatic (bactericidal at high concentration)
- Anti-inflammatory effects (reduces neutrophil chemotaxis) — used in some inflammatory dermatoses
- Motilin receptor agonist → GI cramps

## Pharmacokinetics
- Destroyed by gastric acid — given as enteric-coated base, stearate or estolate (estolate best absorbed)
- Metabolised by CYP3A4 (and inhibits it strongly); poor CSF penetration

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Penicillin-allergic patients: streptococcal and staphylococcal skin infections, erysipelas
- STIs in pregnancy or penicillin/tetracycline allergy: chlamydia, chancroid, LGV, donovanosis
- Erythrasma, pitted keratolysis, acne in pregnancy and children under 8
- Bullous pemphigoid (with nicotinamide), pityriasis rosea (controversial, early use)
- Topical 2% gel/solution: acne (always with BPO — resistance very high), erythrasma

## Dose & formulations
- 500 mg four times daily (30–50 mg/kg/day in children)
- Chlamydia: 500 mg four times daily × 7 days; chancroid: 500 mg three times daily × 7 days; LGV: 500 mg four times daily × 21 days
- Topical 2–4% once or twice daily with BPO

## Adverse effects
- GI cramps, nausea, diarrhoea (motilin effect) — the main problem
- Cholestatic hepatitis (mainly estolate; more in pregnancy)
- QT prolongation, transient hearing loss with high IV doses
- Infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis when given to young infants
- Topical: dryness; resistant C. acnes and staphylococci

## Contraindications
- Liver disease (estolate); long QT
- Concurrent CYP3A4 substrates with serious toxicity: simvastatin/lovastatin, pimozide, ergotamine, terfenadine/astemizole

## Drug interactions
- Strong CYP3A4 inhibitor: raises cyclosporine, tacrolimus, carbamazepine, warfarin, theophylline, statins, colchicine, benzodiazepines
- Topical erythromycin and clindamycin antagonise each other (same 50S site)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Base and stearate are safe in pregnancy; avoid estolate (hepatotoxicity). Note: erythromycin does not adequately treat fetal syphilis.

## Viva points
- Estolate → cholestatic hepatitis
- CYP3A4 inhibitor — cyclosporine and statin interactions
- Safe acne antibiotic in pregnancy/children (oral)
- Topical erythromycin — high resistance; always add BPO

_Sources: Khopkar ch.1 (Macrolides — erythromycin; Table 1.6) and ch.18; Wolverton 4e ch.9 and ch.41. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
